correction.text: metropolitan France and the French Americas of the 1939 Third Republic shape, without Alsace-Lorraine; the German-occupied north and Atlantic coast and the Italian sliver are hatched by the ledger's occupation events

keyframe_review.note: Cliopatria's 356,691 km2 shape for 1940-1942 is the free zone (gazetteer overlay: the unoccupied southern departments, Corsica, French Guiana, Guadeloupe and Martinique) and matches the page's 'unoccupied southern portion of Metropolitan France'. But the French State claimed all of France: 'Paris remained the de jure capital' and 'Alsace-Lorraine was officially still part of France, because the Reich never annexed the region'. Under the occupation rule (hatched, not transferred) the occupied north and the Atlantic coast belong in the shape with an occupation tint, so the shape grows. The page gives no area to compare. This is a judgement call, flagged for the reviewer.

correction.text: metropolitan France with Corsica, without Alsace-Lorraine and without the Americas; occupied by Germany from 11 November 1942 for the former free zone

keyframe_review.note: The 89,011 km2 shape holds only French Guiana, Guadeloupe and Martinique, which joined Free France in the first months of 1943 (Cliopatria draws them as the Free French shape from 1944). After the occupation of the free zone, though, Vichy 'continued its existence as a puppet government within Occupied France' and kept 'nominal civil authority over Metropolitan France except Alsace-Lorraine'. The shape to use is metropolitan France, hatched under German occupation (and Italian in Corsica and the Riviera to September 1943).

The shape is the same as 1943: metropolitan France, occupied, liberated from June and ended by the Ordinance of 9 August 1944.

ledger.note: 10 July 1940: the Vichy regime begins. The National Assembly 'voted to give full powers to Pétain on 10 July 1940' by 569 votes to 80; infobox '10 July 1940 – 9 August 1944'. The armistice of 22 June 1940 left the 'unoccupied southern portion of Metropolitan France', the 'Unoccupied Zone', to the new government at Vichy.

ledger.note: July 1940: the north and the Atlantic coast are German-occupied. The armistice of 22 June 1940 set the Line of Demarcation; the French State kept de jure sovereignty with Paris its nominal capital. The occupation dates from the invasion (the Nazi Germany dossier has June 1940); it is recorded here from the birth of the state.

ledger.note: June 1940 to September 1943: 'a sliver of French territory in the Alps was under direct Italian administration'. The page does not name the communes; the region is a band along the Franco-Italian frontier inside the free zone.

ledger.note: 11 November 1942: the Germans occupy the free zone. Case Anton: 'By the evening of 11 November, German tanks had reached the Mediterranean coast'; the Vichy France page: 'On 11 November 1942, following the landing of the Allies in North Africa'. Vichy's army was disbanded but the regime 'continued its existence as a puppet government'.

First months of 1943: the Americas leave Vichy. French Guiana, Guadeloupe and Martinique 'finally joined Free France in the first months of 1943'.

wars.name: Case Anton

zones.text: the unoccupied southern zone with Corsica, without the Americas

wars.outcome: Germany and Italy occupy the unoccupied zone on 11-12 November 1942; Vichy's Armistice Army is disbanded and the regime survives as a puppet; the fleet at Toulon is scuttled on 27 November.
wars.note: Vichy offered no fight; listed because it moved the border of control.

wars.name: Syria-Lebanon campaign
wars.outcome: Vichy forces lose to the British Empire and Free French in a campaign of 8 June to 14 July 1941 (ceasefire 12 July, Convention of Acre 14 July).
wars.note: The mandate has its own Cliopatria row and dossier (french-mandate-for-syria-and-lebanon); no zone of the Vichy shape changed.

wars.name: Battle of Gabon
wars.outcome: Vichy Gabon is occupied by force between 27 October and 12 November 1940.
wars.note: Gabon is in Cliopatria's French Africa row, not in the Vichy shape; the land change is the Free French dossier's.

wars.name: Operation Menace (Battle of Dakar)
wars.outcome: Repulsed: the Royal Navy and Free French launched Operation Menace on 23 September 1940 and withdrew on 25 September.

certainty.note: The demarcation line of the armistice of 22 June 1940 and the 11 November 1942 occupation are dated and fixed on the map; the Alpine sliver under Italian administration has no stated limits.

notes:
Page budget (1-2) exceeded: four pages, two of them shared with free-french (Free France, Syria-Lebanon campaign).

Cliopatria problems: the 1940-1942 shape draws only the unoccupied zone, Corsica and the Americas and so leaves the German-occupied north out of the French State altogether, while the Nazi Germany dossier (eu-21 a to c) records it as occupied Vichy land; this dossier follows the occupation rule and corrects the shapes to the whole of metropolitan France without Alsace-Lorraine. The 1943 shape (French Guiana, Guadeloupe, Martinique) is the Americas that left Vichy in early 1943 and is wrong for Vichy; Cliopatria has no 1944 shape (the '(Vichy France)' umbrella runs to 1944). Alsace-Lorraine is left out of every Vichy shape: the page says the Reich 'effectively annexed' it though 'officially still part of France'; the Nazi Germany dossier records a 1940 gain from the French Third Republic and a 1944 loss to the same.

Not settled: the colonies. The French African empire (Madagascar to 1942, French West Africa to November 1942, Indochina to 9 March 1945, Syria and Lebanon to 1941, Djibouti to 1942) sits in other Cliopatria rows (French Africa, French Indochina, the mandate); the Free French and Vichy dossiers record only the losses to Free France that Cliopatria's shapes support. The Pacific colonies and French India (summer 1940) are claimed by free-french with vichy-france as counterpart; there is no matching loss here because they are in no Vichy shape. The liberation dates of 1944 (Paris 25 August on other pages) are not on the pages opened, hence confidence 1 for the two occupation_end events. A gap-filler should open Liberation of France and Battle of Normandy.
Region names: 'Alsace' and 'Corsica' resolve; the French Riviera is read as the Alpes-Maritimes coast and the Italian sliver as a one-cell border band, because no page names the communes.
